IBM has announced prototype “quantum fridges” that cool qubits to temperatures roughly 200 times lower than deep‑space (~13 mK). The extreme cryogenic environment suppresses thermal noise, a key step toward error‑corrected, fault‑tolerant quantum computation. According to Live Science, these devices may shorten the time needed to scale practical quantum processors.
